review_status: Evidence reviewed 2026-11-17. NOAA/IUCN and 2024 Bering Sea trawl sources support broad depth and cold near-bottom habitat, but do not validate satellite SST.

profile.size: Min limit 12 inches TL / Bag limit 2-6 per harvester / day
profile.diet: Small fish, crustaceans, squids, and pelagic prey
profile.behavior: Navigates West Coast kelp forests, rocky reefs, and coastal upwelling zones.

factors.reason_template: Water is {value} C, inside preferred Pacific temperature range for rock greenling.
factors.value_notes: The 2024 southwestern Bering Sea trawl study reports rock greenling catches at near-bottom temperatures of 0.5-3.8 °C, but these are bottom-water measurements from winter/spring, not satellite SST or a preferred surface-temperature curve. NOAA and IUCN describe nearshore/intertidal habitat and seasonal depth migration but do not establish a numeric SST preference. The configured 6-14 °C / 8-12 °C SST bands remain unsupported; keep values unchanged and mark needs_source.

factors.reason_template: Depth is {value} m, within prime Pacific depth zone for rock greenling.
factors.value_notes: NOAA/IUCN report rock greenling commonly in nearshore rocky/kelp habitat to about 50 m, but with records to 665 m. A 2024 Bering Sea trawl study found winter/spring catches at 134-498 m and a seasonal return toward the shelf in April-May. The configured 1-30 m range captures shallow habitat but not the species' seasonal deeper distribution; the 3-25 m ideal is not universal.

text.day: Full daylight when Pacific gamefish actively hunt.
